beginner.headline: Nigella Lawson Joins Bake Off as New Judge
beginner.brief: Nigella Lawson is a new judge on The Great British Bake Off. Many critics praised her new role. The show returns to TV later this month. She is taking over from Dame Prue Leith. New contestants are confirmed for the 17th series. A doctor and a hairdresser are among the contestants.

intermediate.headline: Nigella Lawson Joins Great British Bake Off as New Judge
intermediate.brief: TV chef Nigella Lawson has been praised by critics for her new role as a judge on The Great British Bake Off, which returns to Channel 4 later this month. Lawson is taking over from Dame Prue Leith, who said she was leaving the series in order to "work less and play more." The Times said that "lashings of Nigella Lawson help everyone rise to the occasion", while the Telegraph declared "she is more delectable than anything the contestants could whip up in a showstopper challenge". Contestants for the 17th series have also been confirmed, including a paediatric doctor, a competitive sprinter, a hairdresser and a drag artist. Ben Dowell of the Times picked out some of Lawson's lines from the first episode, including "I want it really sumptuous", which he wrote was delivered "in that - there is no other word for it - highly seductive voice of hers". "You can tell the production team are pleased to have her - at times... it feels as if the programme is entertaining royalty," Dowell continued, adding: "Bake Off has found a new star." The Telegraph's Anita Singh concurred, writing: "Nigella is heaven for social media. The woman is a walking meme factory." A competitive sprinter, Moyin, 22, from Essex, balances his studies with athletics and enjoys using flavours inspired by his Nigerian heritage. Yannis, 28, a paediatric doctor from London, wants to challenge the stigma that Bangladeshi men don't belong in the kitchen.

advanced.headline: Nigella Lawson Joins Bake Off: A C1-Higher Analysis of Critical Acclaim and New Contestants
advanced.brief: TV chef Nigella Lawson has been praised by critics for her new role as a judge on The Great British Bake Off, which returns to Channel 4 later this month. Lawson is taking over from Dame Prue Leith, who expressed her departure from the series as a desire to 'work less and play more'. The 17th series officially premieres on 22 September, though its opening episode was screened to critics earlier this week. The Times lauded Lawson's engaging presence, stating that 'lashings of Nigella Lawson help everyone rise to the occasion,' while the Telegraph found her 'more delectable than anything the contestants could whip up in a showstopper challenge'. The roster of contestants for the new series has also been officially confirmed, comprising a paediatric doctor, a competitive sprinter, a hairdresser, and a drag artist. Ben Dowell of the Times specifically highlighted some of Lawson's evocative lines from the debut episode, such as her wish for a bake to be 'really sumptuous,' delivered in her 'highly seductive voice'. Dowell further noted the production team's evident delight in having her, commenting, 'at times... it feels as if the programme is entertaining royalty,' and concluding that 'Bake Off has found a new star'. Anita Singh of The Telegraph similarly concurred, observing that 'Nigella is heaven for social media. The woman is a walking meme factory,' underscoring her inherent appeal for generating online content. Singh further quoted Lawson's distinctive utterances, including 'The flavours are giving me a lot of pleasure,' 'I like a bit of goo,' and 'I'm hoping to find that wonderful frisson.' Among the latest crop of aspiring star bakers is Clara, a marketing graduate from Portugal who only started baking two years ago. Connie, an NHS hospital discharge lead, is affectionately known as 'the cake lady' and utilises baking as a therapeutic means to unwind after demanding days. Gabe, a 32-year-old artist and drag king, developed an early fascination with baking after watching the initial series of Bake Off at thirteen. Moyin, a political economy student and accomplished competitive sprinter, creatively infuses his bakes with flavours inspired by his rich Nigerian heritage. Yannis, a paediatric doctor working in a busy NICU, aspires to dismantle the misconception that Bangladeshi men do not belong in culinary spaces, often brightening his ward with his baking creations.
